complexity.notes: The whole strint class with its recursive __gt__ is over-engineered: the bound strings have a fixed 10-digit length, so the recursion and substring copying can never exceed that, but ||Python integers are arbitrary precision, so the 32-bit restriction can simply be ignored and the reversed value compared with a plain int comparison||, collapsing this to a few lines. Even staying with strings, ||direct lexicographic comparison of equal-length strings is built into Python||, so the recursive hand-rolled comparator is redundant.
complexity.summary: Wraps the input in a custom string-backed integer class, reverses the digit string, and lexicographically compares it against the string forms of the 2^31 bounds to decide whether to return 0 or the signed reversed value.
